To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the presence of mindfulness, a nonreactive awareness of the present moment, is associated with positive psychological outcomes in psychotherapy and (2) the presence of unconditioned presence, a nonreactively aware presence in which there is a sense of being at home with whatever is happening, is associated with the most positive outcomes in psychotherapy.

(a) the presence of the therapist is an essential ingredient of the therapeutic process; and (b) the presence of a therapist who is mindful of the patient’s inner process and who is not caught in his or her own inner process (i.e., who is able to remain mindful of the patient) is the most effective presence.

(1) the therapeutic relationship is the primary factor in determining outcome in therapy, and that (2) the quality of that relationship is determined by the quality of the therapist’s presence, and that (3) this presence is a function of the therapist’s level of mindfulness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the therapeutic relationship in Existential Integrative Psychotherapy and its relationship with the therapeutic process.
the nature of therapeutic presence and the ways in which this is related to the therapeutic process.
the question of how the therapist's unconditioned presence can be cultivated in psychotherapy, and how the play of unconditioned presence may be understood and utilized in psychotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nondual potential of unconditioned presence, as the heart of existential psychotherapy, is the play of empty openness.
the therapeutic relationship is a field of open, unconditioned, nondual awareness, in which the therapist's own unconditioned presence is the essential ingredient.
a therapeutic presence of unconditioned openness, or play, is the most fundamental therapeutic resource in Existential Integrative Psychotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the play of unconditioned presence is a nondual, nonreferential therapeutic presence that is the basis of a new, nondual psychotherapy.

we have been attempting to articulate an experiential, nondual, and transpersonal psychotherapy, which, while rooted in the existential and phenomenological traditions of Western thought, has been informed by the nondual, experiential understanding of Buddhist psychology.
we seek to help clients become more mindful of the unconditioned presence in their lives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nondual potential of the therapeutic relationship is the most effective means of facilitating the healing and transformation of clients.

the therapeutic process, as well as the psychotherapist's own development, can be seen in the light of the play of empty openness, which can be seen to be the ground, the process, the result, and the goal of psychotherapy.
the nonduality of sunyata is the most potent and transformative therapeutic presence.
